clue.text: Meant to get lower classes free

parts.note: D and E are the lowest grades in the British social classification of occupations
to free is to liberate, a verb in the same form

explanation.surface: Someone wants the lower classes to be set free.
explanation.walkthrough: D and E are the bottom bands of the UK's ABC1 social grading, used by marketers and pollsters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something meant was done on purpose, a synonym for intentional.

clue.text: Female captivates very peaceful type

indicators.note: captivates is read as captures, so the female holds the other letter within

parts.note: a doe is a female deer or rabbit

explanation.surface: A woman completely charms a gentle soul.
explanation.definitionFit: In politics a pacifist or one who favours negotiation is called by this bird's name, the symbol of peace.

clue.text: Rang a salad bar up reserving pasta dish

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters read from bottom to top, backwards
reserving means keeping within, so the letters sit inside the words

explanation.surface: Someone phoned a salad bar to reserve a pasta dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reserving' holds ANGASAL in 'Rang a salad'; 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: This baked dish of flat pasta sheets layered with sauce is a classic Italian pasta dish.

clue.text: British hail American dystopian novel

parts.note: ave is a Latin greeting, hail
the New World is the Americas, so American suggests it

explanation.surface: A Brit greets an American who loves bleak fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldous Huxley's 1932 book depicts a controlled future society, a classic dystopia.

clue.text: Subject of jokes in actual denial

indicators.note: in places the first piece within the second

parts.note: real means actual
the butt of jokes is their target

explanation.surface: The target of the jokes actually denies it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuttal is a contradiction or refutation of a claim.

clue.text: Singer from English National Opera visiting Turkey

indicators.note: visiting means calling in, so the company goes inside

parts.note: TR is the international vehicle code for Turkey
ENO is the abbreviation of English National Opera, a London company

explanation.surface: A singer from a London opera company visits Turkey on tour.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenor is a male singer with a high voice.

clue.text: Cooker right to make jelly

parts.note: an Aga is a British brand of heavy cast-iron range cooker

explanation.surface: A cook uses the right stove to set a jelly.
explanation.walkthrough: An AGA is a big British range cooker found in country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar is a gelatinous substance from seaweed used to set foods and culture media.

clue.text: When weather is miserable it sounds first-class

indicators.note: it sounds signals a phrase that is pronounced the same as the next one

parts.note: grade A means first-class, top quality

explanation.surface: A paradox: miserable weather is described as first-class.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull overcast day is the time when the weather is gloomy.

clue.text: Rebellion lacking enthusiasm for old comedy programme

parts.note: a rising is an uprising or rebellion
damp means dull, lacking enthusiasm, as in a damp squib

explanation.surface: A revolt fizzles out for lack of spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: Rising Damp was a 1970s ITV sitcom set in a shabby boarding house.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1970s British sitcom starring Leonard Rossiter is an old comedy programme.

clue.text: Prospect of time filling in travel document

indicators.note: the time letter fills a gap within the travel document, so it sits inside it

parts.note: a visa is an endorsement in a passport allowing entry

explanation.surface: Someone is filling in a travel form and has to give the time.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect is a view stretching away, the same as a vista.

clue.text: Rails bearing one by top of stairs?

definitions.text: Rails bearing one by top of stairs?

indicators.note: something bearing a thing carries it within itself, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: to rail at someone is to jeer or mock, much as one banters
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A description of handrails that hold you up as you reach the top of a flight of stairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing' puts I and S (the top of 'stairs') inside BANTERS. Read whole, the clue also describes the handrails beside a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: Handrails running beside a staircase, supporting a climber up to the landing, are what this item is.

clue.text: Filming top actors — they have meteoric careers

parts.note: shooting a film means filming it
the leading actors are the stars

explanation.surface: Filming leading actors whose careers have taken off fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Meteors streak across the sky, so their careers are literally meteoric; a playful definition.

clue.text: Garden role not adapted by urban area

indicators.note: adapted means altered into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor's role in a stage garden is changed by an urban setting.
explanation.definitionFit: The administrative region covering the whole British capital and its boroughs is a large urban area.

clue.text: Shield wounded guerrilla imprisoned by flipping beak

indicators.note: imprisoned by means held inside the following piece
flipping means turning over, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: beak is slang for nose
cut means wounded
Che Guevara was the famous Argentine guerrilla leader

explanation.surface: A wounded guerrilla is held by a flipping magistrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' and 'imprisoned by' do the work here. 'Beak' looks like British slang for a magistrate, which fits the prison picture, but here it means the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry this is the shield-shaped surface bearing a coat of arms.

clue.text: Pointless friend losing head and gathering speed for Armstrong, perhaps?

indicators.note: gathering means collecting something up inside, so the other piece goes within
losing its head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: Richard Osman is co-presenter of the BBC quiz show Pointless alongside his friend Alexander Armstrong
pace is a synonym for speed

explanation.surface: A puzzle for quiz fans: Armstrong's sidekick on Pointless loses his head and speeds up.
explanation.walkthrough: Pointless is a BBC quiz hosted by Alexander Armstrong with Richard Osman. 'losing head' drops O to leave SMAN, and 'gathering' puts PACE inside. 'Armstrong' then switches to Neil, the astronaut.
explanation.definitionFit: Neil Armstrong, the first man on the Moon, is an example of an astronaut.

clue.text: Remained sober as reported

indicators.note: as reported means as heard spoken, signalling a word of the same sound

parts.note: staid means sober and sedate

explanation.surface: Someone stayed sober, according to the report.
explanation.definitionFit: Remained and stayed are synonyms in the past tense.

clue.text: Company brought up articles about improving superficial appearance

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: items are articles or things
C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A firm's articles about improving one's looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic describes treatment that improves only the surface look of something.

clue.text: Residential area as far as the outskirts of Wigan

parts.note: up to means as far as, a preposition phrase

indicators.note: the outskirts of a word are its outer letters

explanation.surface: Housing estates sprawl as far as the edge of Wigan, a town in north-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the outskirts of' takes the first and last letters of Wigan, W and N.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage the more residential part of a city, away from the business district, is so called.

clue.text: Camping equipment — something to bowl at, taking wicket ultimately

indicators.note: taking means taking in, holding the letter inside

parts.note: a tenpin is a skittle knocked over in bowling

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, the last letter

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler aims at the stumps and takes a wicket at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives T from 'wicket'; 'taking' puts it inside TENPIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A peg used to secure a tent to the ground is part of camping gear.

clue.text: Mother crossing on old airline gets night light

indicators.note: crossing here means stretching across and around the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: mom is an informal word for mother
BEA was British European Airways, a former UK airline

explanation.surface: Mother gets on an old airliner for a night flight.
explanation.walkthrough: BEA, British European Airways, merged into British Airways in 1974.
explanation.definitionFit: A ray of moonlight is a light seen at night.

clue.text: Surround space nearby

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of space
close means nearby

explanation.surface: Fill the nearby space all round.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a printer's measure of width, so 'space' can mean EN.
explanation.definitionFit: To enclose something is to fence it in on all sides.

clue.text: Avant-garde recordings could be so … um … eccentric

indicators.note: could be signals that these letters may be made into something else by rearranging

explanation.surface: A hesitant listener finds experimental recordings, um, rather eccentric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges SO, UM and ECCENTRIC; the hesitant 'um' hides useful letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Musique concrete is experimental music built from recorded natural sounds, an avant-garde genre.

clue.text: Support article that's reduced effective powers

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A supporting piece reports how something's real powers were cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeth means the power to enforce, as in a law with no bite.

clue.text: Stupid person preserved beef

definitions.meaning: an idiot or fool, in informal speech
meat cut into strips and dried to keep, as in the dish called jerky

explanation.surface: An idiot munching dried beef.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for a fool and also names meat cured by drying, the base of jerky.

clue.text: Old fusspot forgetting answer — that is coming in handy

parts.note: ex means former or old

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so the abbreviation sits inside the other piece
forgetting something means leaving it out

parts.note: a pedant fusses over small details
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: An old stickler forgets the answer, which turns out handy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgetting' removes the answer's abbreviation from the fusspot, and 'coming in' signals the insertion. 'Old' is EX, as in an ex-wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedient means convenient and useful for the purpose, near enough synonymous with handy.

clue.text: In agreement to make amends

definitions.meaning: being ... with someone means agreeing with them
to make amends is to make up for a wrong

explanation.surface: Reconciled parties agree to make up for past wrongs.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means united in opinion; as one word it means to expiate a wrong.

clue.text: Number regularly found in Indian tea

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A numeral turns up in an Indian tea blend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly found in' takes the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters of 'Indian tea'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine is a whole number, a cardinal numeral.

clue.text: Throws away meal given king — not the finest cut of meat

definitions.text: not the finest cut of meat

parts.note: chucks means throws away or discards
tea is an evening meal in parts of Britain
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Someone throws out a dinner served to the king because the meat is a poor cut.
explanation.walkthrough: In much of Britain 'tea' is the name for the evening meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Chuck is a cheaper cut from the shoulder of beef, tough and suited to stewing.
